time.desc: The leader of one party issued a time-limited ultimatum to his opponent through social platforms, demanding the resumption of commercial shipping in key straits and threatening to attack the other party's power and other energy facilities.
The adversary's military forces issued a statement stating that if they were attacked on their energy facilities, they would take escalating measures and completely close the key strait.
One party announced that it had opened dialogue with its opponent and promised to temporarily suspend attacks on the other party's energy facilities in exchange for a diplomatic window.
One party formally submits a ceasefire/end-of-conflict plan containing multiple clauses to its opponent to push for a breakdown in negotiations.
The opponent completed and submitted a formal response to the multi-term ceasefire plan, marking the next stage of ceasefire negotiations.
The two parties joined forces to carry out military strikes on port/terminal targets close to key straits and caused casualties.
The two countries outside the region jointly proposed an alternative ceasefire plan, calling for an immediate ceasefire and the restoration of normal traffic in key straits.

The leader of one of the parties involved in the war publicly called on all countries to go to the key strait to rush to transport oil, claiming that the opponent had been basically defeated, and related oil prices rose sharply late at night.

The leader of one side delivered a nationally televised address announcing that he would carry out harsher military strikes against his opponents in the coming weeks and claimed to strive to end the conflict within a few weeks.
The two sides launched joint air strikes on their opponents’ important petrochemical industrial parks and export port-related facilities.
One side publicly threatened to bomb the opponent's civilian infrastructure such as power plants and bridges on a specific date and once again demanded the opening of key straits.
One side agreed to implement a ceasefire/bombing moratorium on its opponents for approximately two weeks to mitigate the risk of escalation.
Relevant allies publicly stated that the ceasefire arrangement did not restrict their actions against third-party armed forces, triggering disputes over the scope of the ceasefire.
Opponents held large-scale commemorations for forty days after the death of the supreme leader. The successor supreme leader said that his country shocked the world during the war.

The navy of one of the participating parties began to mobilize troops to key straits and prepare to blockade the opponent's ports. The actions were carried out at the same time as the talks between the two sides.
The military of one party officially launched a naval blockade of the opponent's port and stated that it would not affect the freedom of navigation of non-opponent port ships through key straits.
